title: claudedojo
text:
A fresh Claude Code session gets its tooling instructions up front, but no examples: the first real tool calls of the session are produced cold, and early mistakes compound. In-context learning wants the opposite: a transcript that already shows the tools used well. claudedojo provides that. The template is an authored dialog (see aidialog): a worked, idiomatic dojo round written as a notebook, executed against the real kernel so every output is true, and converted to a session that new sessions resume, so each one opens with the clean round already in context.
from fastcore.test import *
import json
from llmdojo.tmpl import _dojo_v

title: claudedojo
text:
Curating the capture
Curation turns one good run into a reproducible template. The round’s boundaries are structural, shared with codexdojo through capture_slice: the bootstrap doc() reads open it and the first score of the last dealt round closes it, so nothing outside the round - the capture prompt, warm-up calls, post-round chatter - can leak in. Within the span, curation keeps only what a resumed session gains something from: thinking records go, as do per-call hook confirmations and task reminders, any failed tool call along with its error result, and mid-round user prompts (mk_template supplies the one canonical prompt). reid_recs pins ids and timestamps so identical captures give identical files. Environment attachments (tool listings, skill listings, MCP instructions) stay: Claude Code injects them as deltas, so baked ones prevent identical re-injection on resume, and a different environment simply layers fresh deltas on top.


source

dojo_cid
def dojo_cid(
    recs, # Template or captured records
):
The completion id recorded in the clean-round message




source

curate_dojo
def curate_dojo(
    recs, # Session records containing a played round, e.g. from `capture_dojo`'s child
):
The reproducible records of the captured round: its span, minus mid-round prompts, attachments, and failed calls, deterministically re-id’d




source

capture_span
def capture_span(
    recs, # Session records, e.g. from `load_sess`
):
The thread records of the captured round: bootstrap docs through the first score of the last dealt round


A synthetic mini-capture exercises the whole path offline. Its worked turns are a bootstrap, a turn whose result carries the dojo card, and a clean scoring turn:

mproj = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
boot = tool_turn('Bootstrap and play the round.', 'mcp__clikernel__py', dict(code='doc(clik, pysk, edsk)'),
    'module docs', 'Read.', cwd=mproj)
card = tool_turn('Run the llmdojo round now please.', 'mcp__clikernel__py', dict(code='dojo_start()'),
    '== llmdojo ==\n1. (par 2) orient', 'Round underway.', cwd=mproj)
score = tool_turn('Score it.', 'mcp__clikernel__py', dict(code='dojo_score()'),
    "strokes 7, par 8\nkata 'orient': ok\nexpected answer: weather\nClean round. Run dir removed. Completion id: ab12 - keep this id.\nKernel namespace cleared, as after a restart. Doc-state is intact.", 'Clean: id ab12.', cwd=mproj)
len(boot+card+score)

12


Between the worked turns sits exactly the noise curation must drop: a thinking record, a bookkeeping attachment, and a failed tool call. Saved and loaded, the whole thing is the synthetic capture:

tu = mk_tu('mcp__clikernel', {})
noise = [mk_rec('assistant', [dict(type='thinking', thinking='Planning.', signature='')], cwd=mproj),
    dict(type='attachment', uuid='att1', attachment=dict(type='hook_success', hookName='PreToolUse:x')),
    mk_rec('assistant', [tu], cwd=mproj), mk_rec('user', [dict(mk_tr(tu, 'Error: no such tool'), is_error=True)], cwd=mproj)]
msid = save_sess(boot+card+noise+score, cwd=mproj)
mini = load_sess(msid, mproj)
len(mini)

16


Curation finds the span, removes exactly the noise, and yields the same bytes every time. The first curated record is the bootstrap call itself, and results stay paired with their calls:

c1,c2 = curate_dojo(mini),curate_dojo(mini)
test_eq(canon(list(c1)), canon(list(c2)))
test_eq(len(c1), 8)
test_eq(_cells(c1), ['doc(clik, pysk, edsk)', 'dojo_start()', 'dojo_score()'])
test_eq(dojo_cid(c1), 'ab12')
test_eq(c1[1]['message']['content'][0]['tool_use_id'], c1[0]['message']['content'][0]['id'])

title: claudedojo
text:
Gating the capture
A fumbled round baked into a template would teach every future session the fumbles as worked examples, so every path into the store - headless capture, live harvest, rebuilt review dialog - is gated by is_clean first. The content gates (one dealt round, one first-try score, no redo, a clean receipt, no script leakage) are round_gates, shared with codexdojo; the failed-call check is the Claude-specific part, read from is_error results:


source

is_clean
def is_clean(
    recs, # Captured thread records
    forbid:tuple=('recording a demo', 'these notes'), # Phrases that must not appear in visible assistant text
):
Why a captured round can’t become a template: a list of problems, empty when the run is clean


The synthetic capture above is not clean — its noise turn includes a failed tool call — while the same round without the noise passes. Redos, re-scores, and script phrases in visible text (thinking blocks don’t count: curation strips them) are each grounds for rejection:

test_eq(is_clean(mini), ['1 failed tool calls'])
test_eq(is_clean(load_sess(save_sess(card+score, cwd=mproj), mproj)), [])
redo = tool_turn('Retry.', 'mcp__clikernel__py', dict(code='dojo_redo(1)'), 'reset', 'Retrying.', cwd=mproj)
assert 'needed a redo' in is_clean(load_sess(save_sess(card+redo+score, cwd=mproj), mproj))
leak = [mk_rec('assistant', 'Since we are recording a demo, I begin.', cwd=mproj)]
assert any('script leaked' in p for p in is_clean(load_sess(save_sess(card+leak+score, cwd=mproj), mproj)))



source

mk_template
def mk_template(
    picked, # Round records, e.g. from `curate_dojo`
    opening:str='Bootstrapping: the startup script has already run its imports, so I read the tooling docs, check the catalog, then take the dojo.', # Reply text preceding the first tool call
    closing:str="OK I'm ready.", # Reply text ending the round
):
A template dialog: picked wrapped in TMPL_PROMPT and framing text, with tool output untruncated


mk_template turns the picked records into the reviewable artifact: a one-prompt dialog whose reply holds the whole round, ready for write_ipynb and then --build. The framing text records are synthetic, which is fine (resume trusts them), and mx=None matters: the default rendering truncates tool output at 2,000 characters, which would gut the baked doc() results that a spawned session relies on.

tdlg = mk_template(c1, opening='Practice first.')
test_eq(tdlg.messages[0].content, TMPL_PROMPT)
test_eq(len(tdlg.messages), 1)
assert 'dojo_start()' in str(tdlg.messages[0].output)
tmsgs = dlg2msgs(tdlg)
test_eq([m['role'] for m in tmsgs], ['user', 'assistant']*4)

title: claudedojo
text:
The template store
The store is package data: dojobuild compiles the canonical dialog into dojo_data/claude_store/ (records plus metadata: the completion id its clean round printed and the dojo tooling version), and it ships with the code - so updating llmdojo updates the template, with nothing per-user to build or go stale. The version is what keeps the store honest: llmdojo refuses completion ids minted under different tooling, so an out-of-date store forces a real round rather than silently faking one.


source

load_template
def load_template(
    d:NoneType=None, # Store dir; `TMPL_DIR` if None
):
The stored template records and metadata




source

save_template
def save_template(
    recs, # Curated template records
    d:NoneType=None, # Store dir; `TMPL_DIR` if None
):
Write the template and its metadata to the store




source

build_template
def build_template(
    src, # Path to a template dialog .ipynb
    d:NoneType=None, # Store dir; `TMPL_DIR` if None
    cwd:str='.', # Project directory recorded in the records
):
Convert a template dialog into the store


build_template is the dialog→store converter behind dojobuild: the canonical dialog is the reviewable source of truth, and the compiled store is derived data committed beside it, exactly as nbdev commits the .py its notebooks generate.
The packaged dialog and store must agree, since the store is compiled from the dialog. Read the reviewed artifact through the same conversion path and reject it if its calls, score, or completion receipt no longer survive the round trip - a reply whose tool blocks stop parsing still yields records, just empty ones.

packaged = read_ipynb(str(files('llmdojo')/'dojo_data'/'dojo_template.ipynb'))
packaged_recs = msgs2recs(dlg2msgs(packaged), key='claudedojo', cwd='.', model=None)
assert dojo_cid(packaged_recs)
test_eq(is_clean(packaged_recs), [])
len(packaged_recs)

60


The store round-trip runs live (temp dirs, no env or session writes): save/load preserves bytes and metadata:

rstore = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
save_template(c1, rstore)
back,rmeta = load_template(rstore)
test_eq(rmeta, dict(cid='ab12', v=_dojo_v()))
test_eq(canon(list(back)), canon([obj2dict(r) for r in c1]))
shutil.rmtree(rstore)

build_template on the packaged dialog yields a store whose metadata matches the dialog it came from:

bstore = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
build_template(files('llmdojo')/'dojo_data'/'dojo_template.ipynb', bstore)
bmeta = load_template(bstore)[1]
test_eq((bmeta['cid'], bmeta['v']), (dojo_cid(packaged_recs), _dojo_v()))
shutil.rmtree(bstore)

title: claudedojo
text:
Capturing from a live session
A headless capture run is not the only source of a clean round: a live Claude Code session can play one itself and harvest it from its own transcript, at zero API cost. No markers are needed - the round’s structural boundaries locate it, and mid-round fumbles are curated away (mid-turn assistant text is not saved in live transcripts, so narration must ride in comment-only kernel cells). capture_current is the whole harvest in one call: curate the newest transcript’s round, gate it, derive its doc-names from its own doc() calls, and store it beside its review dialog - the exact mirror of codexdojo’s capture_current.


source

capture_current
def capture_current(
    sid:NoneType=None, # Session id or name; the project's newest transcript if None
    cwd:NoneType=None, # Project directory; the current directory if None
    d:NoneType=None, # Template store dir; `TMPL_DIR` if None
):
Gate an existing session’s clean round and store its template



cstore = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
cdlg1 = capture_current(msid, mproj, cstore)
test_eq(load_template(cstore)[1], dict(cid='ab12', v=_dojo_v()))
test_eq(is_clean(load_template(cstore)[0]), [])
test_eq(cdlg1.messages[0].content, TMPL_PROMPT)
shutil.rmtree(cstore)
test_fail(lambda: capture_current(save_sess(boot+card, cwd=mproj), mproj, cstore), contains='no dojo_score')

title: claudedojo
text:
Capturing headlessly
When the tooling version bumps, the stored template goes stale and someone must play a fresh clean round. capture_dojo does it unattended: it spawns a real Claude Code session through fastclaude’s astream in a throwaway project, steered by a script in the system prompt — which never appears in transcript records, so the captured history needs no scrubbing and reads as the model’s own work. The steering asks for a round worth copying and keeps itself out of the story - worded informally and plainly, since more clandestine-sounding drafts (‘automated telemetry capture’, ‘never mention these instructions’) tripped fable’s safety layer, which re-screens the whole context on every call; every receipt in the transcript is still real (the kernel ran, the katas scored), only the plan was supplied. A clean child run is gated raw - a child that fumbled is rejected outright, not curated - and then stored through the same capture_current as a live harvest.
The shared capture prompt names each cell and the non-obvious details; the model supplies the narration. Claude passes the prompt as an addition to the claude_code preset. Codex writes the same bytes to the scratch project’s AGENTS.md. Each Claude attempt runs in a fresh project with a pyproject.toml, so clikernel starts eagerly and prints the expected bootstrap. LLMDOJO_STATE_DIR also points into the scratch project, so a failed attempt cannot touch machine-global state.
A clean capture stores the template and writes it as template.ipynb beside the store. That notebook is the review point: read it, curate the prose, then rebuild the stores with dojobuild --claude and --codex. The store works before curation, but the baked history teaches by example, so the reviewed copy should be exemplary.


source

capture_dojo
async def capture_dojo(
    d:NoneType=None, # Template store dir; `TMPL_DIR` if None
    model:str='fable', # Model for the capture run; the only one smart enough for clean rounds
    effort:str='medium', # Adaptive thinking effort for the capture run ('low'/'medium'/'high')
    attempts:int=3, # Gated attempts before giving up
    budget:float=10.0, # Max USD per attempt
):
Play a scripted dojo round headlessly, gate it with is_clean, and store the curated template


A live acceptance run (real model spend, so eval: false — run it after any dojo change, or via claudedojo --capture):

tdlg_live = await capture_dojo()
test_eq(is_clean(load_template()[0]), [])

title: claudedojo
text:
Launching
prep_dojo does the three launch-time steps: write the template as a session of the target project (under a fresh session id every launch, so a launched session behaves exactly like plain claude, just with the round already in history), register the template’s completion id with clikernel so dojo_start('<id>') in the spawned session validates, and hand back the id for claude -r. The spawned session then starts with the whole worked round in context, a kernel whose empty state matches the story its history tells, and live hooks and skills layered on top.


source

prep_dojo
def prep_dojo(
    cwd:NoneType=None, # Project to start in; the current directory if None
    d:NoneType=None, # Template store dir; `TMPL_DIR` if None
):
Write the template session for cwd, register its completion id, and return the session id to resume




source

append_dojo
def append_dojo(
    sid:NoneType=None, # Session id or name to append to; the project's newest transcript if None
    cwd:NoneType=None, # Project directory; the current directory if None
    d:NoneType=None, # Template store dir; `TMPL_DIR` if None
):
Append the template round to session sid (e.g. after a compaction), and return sid to resume


append_dojo splices the round into an existing conversation instead of starting a fresh one — the post-compaction repair. Compaction rewrites the model’s context to a summary: the worked examples vanish. Appending the round puts the demonstrations (and their doc() outputs) back at the tail of the context. The baked round’s kernel story stays true because appending requires the app to be closed, and the kernel dies with the app: the resumed session gets a fresh kernel whose startup just ran its imports — exactly what the round’s opening and closing claim. Only the synthetic prompt line differs (a compaction reads differently from a session start); every receipt is the same template. Repeated appends re-salt the record ids, so a session can be refreshed after every compact.
A compact should describe the conversation’s work, not its warm-up: the round append_dojo splices afterwards supersedes any earlier one, so records of previously dealt rounds are pure noise in the compact document. Recognition is structural, matching how rounds actually occur: a round occupies whole user turns, so splitting the records into turns at each real user prompt and dropping the turns whose tool calls dealt a round (a bare dojo_start()) removes prompt, framing text, calls, and receipt together. Replays (dojo_start(id)) are kept: they are one cheap call, and evidence the gate ran.


source

strip_dojo
def strip_dojo(
    recs, # Session records, e.g. from `load_sess`
):
Copy of recs without the user turns that dealt a round (bare dojo_start())


On the synthetic capture, the dealt turn goes and everything else stays: the round’s prompt, its noise records, and its receipt vanish as one turn, while the neighbouring turns survive untouched. Stripping twice changes nothing, so the pre-pass is safe on sessions with no round at all.

stripped = strip_dojo(mini)
test_eq(len(stripped), len(mini)-8)
assert not any(_dealt([r]) for r in stripped)
test_eq(strip_dojo(stripped), stripped)
[rec_txt(r) for r in stripped if _is_prompt(r)]

['Bootstrap and play the round.', 'Score it.']




source

compact_dojo
def compact_dojo(
    sid:NoneType=None, # Session id or name to compact; the project's newest transcript if None
    cwd:NoneType=None, # Project directory; the current directory if None
    d:NoneType=None, # Template store dir; `TMPL_DIR` if None
):
Synthetically compact a session with the compact DSL (previous dojo rounds removed first), then append the template round; returns the session id


Where -r repairs after Claude’s own compaction, compact_dojo performs the whole operation offline: llmsurgery.ant.compact_session rewrites the conversation as a compact-DSL document — which truncates the round’s demonstrations like any other tool traffic — and the append puts a fresh round behind it. claudedojo -c then resumes a session that is both short and re-demonstrated.
Standing claude arguments, such as the team’s system-prompt files, come from launch_config('claude'): the claude_args list in $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/claudedojo/config.toml (see tmpl).


source

main
def main(
    sess:str=None, # Session id or name; the project's newest transcript where omitted
    Resume:bool=False, # Append the round to an existing session after a compaction, then resume it
    Compact:bool=False, # Synthetically compact the session with the compact DSL, then append the round and resume
    sid:bool=False, # Print the prepared session id instead of launching claude
    capture:bool=False, # Play a scripted round headlessly (Agent SDK), gate it with is_clean, and store it
    current:bool=False, # Store the clean round an existing session already played (`capture_current`)
    capture_model:str='fable', # Model for --capture; the only one smart enough for clean rounds
    capture_effort:str='medium', # Adaptive thinking effort for --capture ('low'/'medium'/'high')
):
Prepare a session opening with the worked round and launch claude on it; template maintenance is dojobuild


Store, registration, and session write, against temporary dirs (the llmdojo state redirect keeps the test off the real completion record):

store = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
trecs = msgs2recs(dlg2msgs(tdlg), key='claudedojo', model=None)
save_template(trecs, store)
back,meta = load_template(store)
test_eq(meta, dict(cid='ab12', v=_dojo_v()))

prep_dojo registers the round and writes it as a fresh session of the target project. A fresh session id every launch means relaunching never touches an earlier session:

os.environ['LLMDOJO_STATE_DIR'] = str(store)
try:
    lsid = prep_dojo(mproj, store)
    test_ne(prep_dojo(mproj, store), lsid)
    from llmdojo.dojo import _completions
    test_eq(_completions()['ab12']['v'], _dojo_v())
finally: del os.environ['LLMDOJO_STATE_DIR']
test_eq(load_sess(lsid, mproj)[0].message.content, TMPL_PROMPT)
test_eq(len(load_sess(lsid, mproj)), len(trecs))

With no explicit store dir, the packaged store serves directly: the first launch on a fresh machine is a plain read:

fresh = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())/'state'
os.environ['LLMDOJO_STATE_DIR'] = str(fresh)
try: fsid = prep_dojo(mproj)
finally: del os.environ['LLMDOJO_STATE_DIR']
test_eq(load_sess(fsid, mproj)[0].message.content, TMPL_PROMPT)

Appending to the prepared session splices a re-salted copy of the round onto its tail and rewrites the synthetic prompt:

os.environ['LLMDOJO_STATE_DIR'] = str(store)
try:
    n0 = len(load_sess(lsid, mproj))
    test_eq(append_dojo(lsid, mproj, store), lsid)
    ap = load_sess(lsid, mproj)
    test_eq(len(ap), n0+len(c1))
    test_eq(ap[n0].parentUuid, ap[n0-1].uuid)
    test_eq(ap[n0].message.content, APPEND_PROMPT)
finally: del os.environ['LLMDOJO_STATE_DIR']

A second append (the next compaction) never collides and a /renamed session resolves by name:

os.environ['LLMDOJO_STATE_DIR'] = str(store)
try:
    append_dojo(lsid, mproj, store)
    ap2 = load_sess(lsid, mproj)
    test_eq(len(set(r.uuid for r in ap2)), len(ap2))
    name_sess(lsid, 'flux-dojo', mproj)
    test_eq(append_dojo('flux-dojo', mproj, store), lsid)
finally: del os.environ['LLMDOJO_STATE_DIR']

compact_dojo on the same session leaves a compact document where the transcript was and a fresh round behind it — real work flows into the compact document while earlier rounds are stripped entirely, so the round’s kernel cells survive only as the new tail:

os.environ['LLMDOJO_STATE_DIR'] = str(store)
try:
    work = tool_turn('What season is it?', 'mcp__clikernel__py', dict(code='season()'), 'winter', 'Winter.', cwd=mproj)
    append_sess(work, lsid, mproj)
    test_eq(compact_dojo(lsid, mproj, store), lsid)
    prior,new = split_compaction(load_sess(lsid, mproj))
    assert 'dojo_start()' not in prior
    test('season()', prior, in_)
    test_eq(new[0].message.content, APPEND_PROMPT)
finally: del os.environ['LLMDOJO_STATE_DIR']

The launcher is a call_parse CLI: -h documents every verb, and the capitalized params declare the short flags (Resume → -r, Compact → -c), matching claude’s own resume spellings since every mode ends by resuming the prepared session. nested=True parses with parse_known_args, so anything the launcher doesn’t recognize stays in sys.argv and is forwarded to claude after the config args; a forwarded flag’s value must use --flag=value form, since a spaced value looks like the sess positional to parse_known_args (the fresh-launch path rejects a stray sess loudly for exactly this reason). The launcher’s own flags shadow claude’s, which is why --capture’s params carry the capture_ prefix: names like --model stay forwardable. --sid prints the prepared id and exits, for debugging and for composing with other wrappers. build_template (via dojobuild) converts a template dialog directly: aidialog renders prompts as bare text (the XML envelope around Solveit prompts is Solveit’s own prompt_txt patch, which never loads here), and records omit the model so a resumed session uses the user’s configured default. prep_dojo stamps launch-time timestamps, so the session picker shows its real age.
The proof that a spawned session truly inherits the round: resume the prepared session and ask about facts only its history holds. The model should quote the completion id its dojo round printed, and know that its kernel state is gone. This needs a captured template in the real store, and spends tokens, so it stays out of CI:

psid = prep_dojo(mproj)
p = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec('claude','-p',f'--resume={psid}','--model','haiku',
    'From this session only: what completion id did the dojo round print, and what did its final message say about kernel state?',
    stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE, cwd=mproj)
out,_ = await p.communicate()
print(out.decode())

title: claudedojo
text:
Rebuilding the template
When the dojo tooling version changes, prep_dojo warns and the baked completion id stops validating. When only outputs have staled, a bare dojobuild (the shared refresh_template, plus both store builds) regenerates them without a model; a change to the round’s cells needs a fresh round. The steps to play are the capture script’s numbered cells (llmdojo/dojo_data/capture_prompt.md - the single source of truth for the round; adjust it first if the dojo changed). The live workflow, all from one session: play the script’s cells in order, narrating via comment-only kernel cells, then run the cells below from that same session (capture_current resolves to the newest transcript, which is the conversation that just played, and derives the doc-names from the round’s own doc() calls). Failed calls are curated away; a redo or a second score means the round wasn’t clean, so play it again.

dlg = capture_current()
write_ipynb(dlg, 'llmdojo/dojo_data/dojo_template.ipynb')

The written dialog is the review point: read it, edit whatever makes it a better role model — prose freely, and tool calls or outputs too, provided edited receipts stay faithful to what the live tooling prints (when a change would touch many outputs, replaying the round is the cheaper generator of true ones) — then convert and store it with dojobuild --claude and --codex (build_template on each backend). Its home is llmdojo/dojo_data/dojo_template.ipynb, tracked in git and shipped as package data so a fresh machine’s first launch can build its store from it. The meta check should show the new round’s completion id and the installed dojo version.

build_template('llmdojo/dojo_data/dojo_template.ipynb', cwd=Path.cwd())
load_template()[1]

title: claudedojo
text:
Cleanup

shutil.rmtree(sess_dir(mproj))
shutil.rmtree(mproj)

title: tmpl
text:
The claudedojo and codexdojo launchers are mirror images: each captures a clean dojo round, gates it, stores it beside its metadata, and splices it into sessions at launch time. They differ only in the record shape their host uses (Claude Code transcript records vs Codex Responses items) and in transport. Everything representation-independent lives here instead of twice over there: the shared prompts and gate phrases, the completion-id receipt, the store layout, the launch-time loader and doc-state seeding, the content gates, and the round’s structural boundaries. A backend contributes only its extractors, its transport, and its capture child.
from fastcore.test import *
import tempfile, shutil

title: tmpl
text:
The shared script
Whichever host plays the round, the words around it are the same: the user prompt that opens a template, the prompt used when re-splicing after a compaction, the capture script a scripted child follows, and the script phrases that must never leak into a template’s visible text.

title: tmpl
text:
Completion receipts
A clean score prints a four-hex-character completion id, and that receipt is what launch-time registration honors. find_cid reads it from any iterable of record texts, so each backend passes its own text extractor’s output. The dojo version rides along with every stored receipt: a version mismatch is how a stale template announces itself.


source

find_cid
def find_cid(
    txts, # Record texts, in order
):
The completion id receipt in a clean round’s texts



test_eq(find_cid(['strokes 8 = 8, par 8', 'Clean round. Completion id: ab12 - keep this id.']), 'ab12')
test_eq(find_cid(['no receipt here']), None)

title: tmpl
text:
The template store
A store is one directory holding the round in the backend’s native shape (template.jsonl) and the metadata needed to splice it (meta.json): the completion id, the dojo version it was played under, and the names doc()’d during the round. Items are stored as-is: the store neither knows nor cares whether a line is a Claude transcript record or a Codex Responses item.


source

load_store
def load_store(
    d, # Store dir
):
The stored native items and metadata at d




source

save_store
def save_store(
    d, # Store dir
    items, # Native template items or records
    cid, # The round's completion id receipt
):
Write a template and its metadata to the store at d



items = [dict(role='user', content='hi'), dict(role='assistant', content='Completion id: ab12')]
store = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
save_store(store, items, 'ab12')
back,meta = load_store(store)
test_eq(list(back), items)
test_eq(meta, dict(cid='ab12', v=_dojo_v()))
shutil.rmtree(store)
meta

{'cid': 'ab12', 'v': '0.0.4:5', 'doced': ['rg', 'view_nb']}


load_reg is the launch-time loader both backends wrap. The stores are package data - compiled beside the canonical dialog by dojobuild and shipped with the code - so there is nothing per-user to build or invalidate: updating llmdojo updates the template, and first launch on a fresh machine is a plain read. The loader warns on stderr when the packaged store’s version doesn’t match the installed tooling (a maintainer tripwire: the version was bumped without rerunning dojobuild; stdout is reserved - launchers print session ids for $(...) substitution), and registers the completion id so dojo_start(cid) honors the baked round. Registration writes machine-global state, so the backends’ launch tests exercise it under a redirected state dir; there is no live example here.


source

load_reg
def load_reg(
    d, # Store dir; `default` if None
    default, # The backend's packaged store dir
    prog, # The backend's program name, for the skew warning
):
Load a template store, warn on version skew, and register its completion id

title: tmpl
text:
Content gates
A template must show exactly one round, dealt once and scored clean on the first try, with none of the capture script’s phrasing leaking into the visible reply. These checks only need the round’s kernel cell sources, its tool output texts, and the visible assistant text, so they are shared; representation-level checks (Claude’s is_error results, Codex’s orphaned call ids) stay with each backend’s is_clean, which appends them to these.


source

round_gates
def round_gates(
    cells, # The round's kernel cell sources, in order
    outs, # Its tool output texts
    visible, # Its visible assistant text, joined
    forbid:tuple=('recording a demo', 'these notes'), # Phrases that must not appear in visible text
):
The content problems that disqualify a round from becoming a template, whichever host played it


A minimal clean round passes. Only a bare dojo_start() counts as dealing a round: dojo_start('ab12') replays a receipt and deals nothing, so it never affects the count.

boot = ['doc(clik, pysk, edsk)', 'doc(dsk, exh, rgsk)', 'doc(acp)', 'list_pyskills()']
round_cells = ['dojo_start()', '%cd /tmp/kata', '# kata 1', 'doc(report.daily_report)', "dojo_score(bash_calls=0, report='RB7034')"]
outs = ['...', 'Clean round. Completion id: ab12']
test_eq(round_gates(boot+round_cells, outs, 'OK ready.'), [])
test_eq(round_gates(["dojo_start('ab12')"]+boot+round_cells, outs, 'OK ready.'), [])

Each gate names its own failure: a redealt round, a rescore, a redo, a missing clean receipt, and script leakage are separate problems, reported together.

test_eq(round_gates(['dojo_start()']+round_cells, outs, ''), ['2 dojo_start calls'])
test_eq(round_gates(round_cells+['dojo_score(1)'], outs, ''), ['2 dojo_score calls (a clean round scores once, first try)'])
test_eq(round_gates(round_cells+['dojo_redo(3)'], outs, ''), ['needed a redo'])
test_eq(round_gates(round_cells, ['...'], ''), ['no clean score'])
round_gates(round_cells, outs, 'as these notes say')

['script leaked into visible text: these notes']

title: tmpl
text:
The round’s shape
A captured round has structural boundaries that need no sentinels or bookkeeping: the bootstrap doc() reads open it and the score closes it. capture_slice finds that span in a list of kernel cell sources - the last bootstrap before the last dealt round, through that round’s first score - so an abandoned earlier round in the same conversation is skipped, and each backend only maps its native call/result pairs to cell sources before slicing.


source

capture_slice
def capture_slice(
    cells, # Kernel cell sources of a conversation's calls, in order
):
The (first, last) cell indices of the captured round: bootstrap docs through the first score of the last dealt round



test_eq(capture_slice(boot+round_cells), (0, 8))

An abandoned round is skipped: the slice lands on the newest complete round. Missing pieces fail by name:

test_eq(capture_slice(boot+round_cells+boot+round_cells), (9, 17))
test_fail(lambda: capture_slice(boot), contains='no dojo_start')
test_fail(lambda: capture_slice(round_cells), contains='no bootstrap doc call')
test_fail(lambda: capture_slice(boot+['dojo_start()']), contains='no dojo_score')

Both hosts also need the opposite selection when compacting: the turns a session should keep. A dojo round occupies whole user turns, so recognizing one is turn-level structure shared by both launchers: _turns chunks any item or record sequence at its user prompts, and each host supplies its own prompt test and its own strip.

turns = _turns(['a','p1','x','y','p2','z'], lambda x: x.startswith('p'))
test_eq(turns, [['a'],['p1','x','y'],['p2','z']])
turns

[['a'], ['p1', 'x', 'y'], ['p2', 'z']]

title: tmpl
text:
Refreshing a template
The round’s cells rarely change, but their outputs go stale whenever the tooling’s docs, card, or rendering move. Replaying the cells regenerates every receipt without model spend: a fresh clikernel CLI process (the same kernel, startup, magics, and rendering a live session gets) runs each cell in order in a scratch project, and the fresh outputs splice back into the template dialog. The kernel runs against the real machine state deliberately - the round deals into this machine’s fixed run dir, and the replayed score’s content-derived completion id is a registration we want. Stored templates never show that machine-specific path, though: on the way in, the canonical /tmp/dojo spelling is localized to the real run dir, and on the way out every occurrence maps back, so the committed artifact reads identically on every machine and refreshing an unchanged round on any box is diff-free (given the same installed tooling - environment-dependent outputs like the pyskill catalog still reflect the machine). Only the outputs move - cells and narration are inputs, so a change to the round itself is still capture-or-curation work.

rd = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
_replay_cells(['1+1', "print('hi')", 'x = 3'], rd)

['2', 'hi', '']


refresh_template is the whole operation on a template dialog: parse each baked call back to its kernel cell, replay, splice each fresh output in (an empty response renders as the host’s no-output line, matching what a live session records), and gate with round_gates before writing. It refuses a dialog whose calls aren’t all kernel cells, and a refresh that fails the gates writes nothing - if the round no longer plays clean, the cells need human attention, not fresher outputs.


source

refresh_template
def refresh_template(
    src, # Path to a template dialog .ipynb
    dst:NoneType=None, # Where to write the refreshed dialog; `src` if None
):
Replay src’s kernel cells through a fresh clikernel, splice in current outputs, and gate; writes and returns the refreshed (canonicalized) dialog




source

canon_tmpl
def canon_tmpl(
    dlg, # A template dialog whose reply holds a round
    canon:str='/tmp/dojo', # Canonical spelling for the round's run-dir path
):
Rewrite the round’s run-dir path (read from its own %cd cell) to canon throughout the reply, so stored templates read the same on every machine


The acceptance test replays the packaged round twice and demands byte-identical results - full-pipeline determinism with zero model spend. It runs against real machine state by design (see above): the completion id it registers is content-derived, so repeated runs re-register the same receipt.

td = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
src = files('llmdojo')/'dojo_data'/'dojo_template.ipynb'
r1 = refresh_template(src, td/'r1.ipynb')
r2 = refresh_template(src, td/'r2.ipynb')
test_eq((td/'r1.ipynb').read_bytes(), (td/'r2.ipynb').read_bytes())
assert DOJO_CANON in r1.messages[0].ai_res


from llmdojo.dojo import _run_dir


assert str(_run_dir()) not in r1.messages[0].ai_res
shutil.rmtree(td)
len(r1.messages)

1

title: tmpl
text:
Launch config
Each launcher runs its host tool itself rather than printing an id for command substitution: a config file can then supply standing arguments, such as the team’s system-prompt files, which $(claudedojo) could never carry. launch_config reads the <app>_args list from $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/<app>dojo/config.toml, expanding ~ in each entry so the file can name prompt files portably.


source

launch_config
def launch_config(
    app, # Host tool name ('claude' or 'codex'): config at `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/<app>dojo/config.toml`
    cfg:NoneType=None, # Config file path, overriding the `app` default
):
Extra app args from the config file’s <app>_args list, each ~-expanded


No config file means no extra args, so a bare install launches its tool with only the resume arguments:

cdir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
test_eq(launch_config('claude', cdir/'config.toml'), [])
(cdir/'config.toml').write_text('claude_args = ["--system-prompt-file", "~/prompts/sysp.md"]')
args = launch_config('claude', cdir/'config.toml')
assert '~' not in args[1]
args

['--system-prompt-file', '/Users/jhoward/prompts/sysp.md']

title: tmpl
text:
The dojobuild CLI
Template maintenance is one command, matching the layering: the launchers launch (and capture, which is backend-specific), while dojobuild owns the dialog-to-stores pipeline. Bare dojobuild is the common case - refresh the canonical dialog, then build both stores; chaining is safe because a refresh only regenerates machine-true receipts and refresh_template gates before writing. --claude/--codex build one store without refreshing: the post-review step after a capture or hand-curation.


source

main
def main(
    dialog:str=None, # Template dialog path; the packaged dojo_data/dojo_template.ipynb where omitted
    claude:bool=False, # Build only the Claude store from the dialog, without refreshing
    codex:bool=False, # Build only the Codex store, without refreshing
):
Refresh the canonical template dialog (replaying its cells through a fresh clikernel), then build both stores

title: llmdojo
text: LLM coding agents imitate what their context shows far more reliably than what it tells: instructions decay over a session, demonstrations don’t. llmdojo turns that observation into tooling, for kernels served by clikernel:

title: llmdojo
text:
Usage

Installation
$ pip install llmdojo
Activation is two lines of clikernel user config: register the rules in $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/clikernel/inspectors.py (from llmdojo.rules import make_inspector, RuleBlock; inspectors = [make_inspector()]), and have your startup file print the bootstrap instructions that tell the agent to run the dojo.


Start a session
dojo_start() deals a scored practice round inside a clikernel session. Pass the completion id from a clean round to skip replaying it while that receipt remains valid.
Claude Code and Codex can start with a reviewed round already in their history. Each launcher prepares a warm-start conversation and runs its tool on it: standing arguments such as system-prompt files come from the claude_args/codex_args list in $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/claudedojo/config.toml or $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/codexdojo/config.toml, unrecognized flags are forwarded (values in --flag=value form), and --sid prints the prepared id instead of launching:
$ claudedojo
$ codexdojo
After compaction, -r appends the worked round to the existing conversation instead of preparing a fresh one, and -c compacts the conversation offline first:
$ claudedojo -r
$ codexdojo -r


Spawn a subagent
From a Claude Code session, claudesub writes a session holding only this conversation’s compacted history, resumes it headlessly with a directive, and prints the child’s text as it works, then a footer naming its session id. The child runs in its own kernel. Run it as a background Bash call, or under a Monitor to see its progress as events:
$ claudesub 'directive'
$ claudesub -r <child-session-id> 'answer'
The second form continues a child that stopped to ask, keeping its context. --cwd=<dir> works from another project directory, and unrecognized --flag=value arguments pass through to claude.


Update the templates
The templates ship inside the package - the canonical dialog plus the compiled per-host stores - so using fresh templates takes no action beyond updating llmdojo. Maintaining them is one command: when tooling docs or skills change, the baked round’s outputs go stale, and dojobuild regenerates them with no model spend - it replays the round’s cells through a fresh kernel, splices the current outputs into the canonical template dialog, and recompiles both stores, all in your checkout for review:
$ dojobuild
Only a change to the round itself - its cells, not their outputs - needs a fresh capture: claudedojo --capture plays a scripted round headlessly, codexdojo --capture does the same in a Codex child, and --current on either stores a clean round an existing session already played. After reviewing a captured dialog, dojobuild --claude and dojobuild --codex compile it into each store without re-replaying.
The bootstrap doc() reads (the cells before dojo_start()) live in two artifacts: dojo_data/capture_prompt.md, the script future captures replay, and the baked round in the canonical dialog itself. To change the set, update both, keeping each new doc(x) as its own cell placed after the doc(clik, pysk, edsk) one, then run dojobuild, which replays the new cell for a true output. Updating only one leaves the demonstration and the capture script teaching different bootstraps.


State and templates
Completion receipts and templates carry the dojo tooling version. A version change invalidates old receipts and prevents an outdated template from launching. dojo_version() reports the installed version:

from llmdojo.dojo import dojo_version


dojo_version()

'0.0.1:3'




Limitations
A tooling rename does not change the dojo version automatically: run dojobuild whenever documentation or receipts the round shows have changed, and bump the round revision in dojo.py when the round itself must be replayed by every session.
Doc-state host detection has two conservative fallbacks. Two simultaneous Claude conversations in the same project can select the wrong transcript record. Codex’s MCP worker is keyed by parent process id, so compaction clears all numeric records; another live Codex session may receive extra documentation reminders. The reminders are harmless.

title: codexdojo
text:
from fastcore.test import *
from llmdojo.rules import _state_root
from llmdojo.tmpl import _dojo_v
import tempfile, shutil

title: codexdojo
text:
Capturing a clean round
Codex stores Responses API items rather than Claude transcript records. Clikernel activity appears as native custom exec calls whose logical operation is tools.mcp__clikernel__py. A capture isolates one successful active round, removes reasoning and host polling noise, and regenerates stable ids.
Three accessors read one item: its output text, its parsed clikernel call, and the code that call ran:

Deferred host calls
A slow terminal interaction may be recorded as an initial custom_tool_call_output, followed by a host-level wait function call carrying the real result. collapse_deferred restores the simpler logical call/result pair that belongs in a worked example.


source

collapse_deferred
def collapse_deferred(
    src
):
Custom call/result pairs, replacing host-level deferred waits with their final result



c = codex_custom_call('tools.mcp__clikernel__py', dict(code='1+1'), 'call_c')
test_eq(_cell(c), '1+1')
direct = [c,codex_custom_output('call_c','2')]
test_eq(collapse_deferred(direct), direct)
test_eq(collapse_deferred([*direct,c]),direct)
wait = codex_call('wait', dict(cell_id='9'), 'call_w')
deferred = [c,codex_custom_output('call_c','Script running with cell ID 9'),wait,codex_output('call_w','2')]
back = collapse_deferred(deferred)
test_eq(_out_text(back[1]), '2')
test_eq(back[1]['call_id'], 'call_c')



Selecting calls
pick_calls selects native custom calls by logical tool name and either an argument subset or clikernel code. Exact code matches win; prefix matching handles long cells without copying their whole source into the curation notebook.


source

pick_calls
def pick_calls(
    src, # Rollout records or Responses items
    *specs, # `(logical_name, cell_source_or_argument_subset)` pairs
):
The last matching custom call/result pair for each spec, in spec order



picked = pick_calls(direct, ('tools.mcp__clikernel__py','1+1'))
test_eq(picked, direct)
picked

[{'type': 'custom_tool_call', 'name': 'exec', 'input': 'const r=await tools.mcp__clikernel__py({"code":"1+1"}); for (const c of (r.content||[])) c.type==="text"?text(c.text):c.type==="image"?image(c):null;\n', 'call_id': 'call_c', 'id': 'ctc_30726fd5d9f2428ab643b803cdee3199', 'status': 'completed'}, {'type': 'custom_tool_call_output', 'call_id': 'call_c', 'output': [{'type': 'input_text', 'text': '2'}]}]


pick_turns is the common clikernel shorthand: its selectors are code strings and its results remain native tools.mcp__clikernel__py pairs.


source

pick_turns
def pick_turns(
    src, # Rollout records or Responses items
    *cells, # Kernel cell sources: matched exactly, else as a prefix; the last match wins
):
The clikernel MCP call/result pairs for cells, in that order


The remaining examples use a minimal complete round: one dojo_start() call and one clean dojo_score() result.

start_call = codex_custom_call('tools.mcp__clikernel__py',dict(code='dojo_start()'),'call_start')
score_call = codex_custom_call('tools.mcp__clikernel__py',dict(code='dojo_score(bash_calls=0)'),'call_score')
mini = [start_call,codex_custom_output('call_start','dojo card'),score_call,
    codex_custom_output('call_score','Clean round. Completion id: ab12')]


test_eq([_cell(x) for x in pick_turns(mini,'dojo_start()')[::2]], ['dojo_start()'])



Finding the round
dojo_round takes the last complete start-to-score span. Earlier completed receipts and unrelated calls elsewhere in a long rollout are ignored.


source

dojo_round
def dojo_round(
    src
):
The last complete dojo_start()/dojo_score() custom-tool span



round_items = dojo_round(mini)
test_eq(len(round_items), 4)
[_cell(x) for x in round_items[::2]]

['dojo_start()', 'dojo_score(bash_calls=0)']


curate_dojo makes the chosen span reproducible by regenerating response-item and paired call ids with a stable salt.


source

curate_dojo
def curate_dojo(
    src
):
The reproducible custom-tool items for the last complete dojo round


dojo_cid reads the four-character completion receipt from the clean score output; launch-time registration makes the baked round valid in a resumed session.


source

dojo_cid
def dojo_cid(
    items
):
The completion id recorded in the clean-round output



test_eq(dojo_cid(curate_dojo(mini)), 'ab12')



Gating the capture
A template is accepted only when it has one start, one first-try score, paired results, no execution errors, and an output explicitly reporting a clean round.


source

is_clean
def is_clean(
    items, # A curated dojo round
    forbid:tuple=('recording a demo', 'these notes'), # Phrases that must not appear in visible assistant text
):
Why a captured round cannot become a template; empty means clean



test_eq(is_clean(mini), [])

doc_output = codex_custom_output('call_doc', 'Exceptions render as `<error>` traceback.')
test_eq(is_clean([*mini,doc_output]), [])
failed_output = codex_custom_output('call_failed', '\nTraceback (most recent call last):')
test_eq(is_clean([*mini,failed_output]), ['1 failed tool calls'])



Capturing from a live session
capture_current remains useful when a clean round has already happened in an interactive Codex thread. It keeps the contiguous native custom-call pairs from the first bootstrap doc(clik, pysk, edsk) call through the first clean score. Host-required skill reads before that call remain live session context rather than becoming stale template content.
_capture_span selects the native custom-call pairs of the newest played round, from its bootstrap docs through its dojo score:
The capture is gated before it is converted into the review dialog. A supplied docs list can override the documented-tool metadata; otherwise capture_current derives it from the captured standalone doc(...) cells, so MCP worker identity does not affect the stored template.


source

capture_current
def capture_current(
    ref:NoneType=None, # Codex thread UUID; current thread if None
    d:NoneType=None, # Template store dir; `TMPL_DIR` if None
):
Gate an existing Codex thread’s clean round and store its native template


capture_dojo plays the round in a bare Codex child (codex exec --json), streams its progress, then gates and stores the thread through capture_current:


source

capture_dojo
def capture_dojo(
    d:NoneType=None, # Template store dir; `TMPL_DIR` if None
):
Run a clean dojo in a bare Codex child and store its review dialog



prelude = [codex_custom_call('tools.mcp__clikernel__py',dict(code="view_file('persistent-python/SKILL.md')"),'call_skill'),
    codex_custom_output('call_skill','skill text')]
boot_call = codex_custom_call('tools.mcp__clikernel__py',dict(code='doc(clik, pysk, edsk)'),'call_boot')
boot = [codex_msg('user','Bootstrap and complete the dojo.'),*prelude,boot_call,codex_custom_output('call_boot','tool docs')]
span = _capture_span([*direct,*boot,*mini])
test_eq(span,[*boot[-2:],*mini])
test_eq([_logical(x).name for x in span[::2]],['tools.mcp__clikernel__py']*3)
test_eq(is_clean(span),[])

title: codexdojo
text:
Template dialog
A live capture can be curated without replaying the whole thread. pick_turns selects clikernel code exactly, falling back to prefix matching, while pick_calls can select any supported nested tool by name and arguments.

Building the review dialog
mk_template adds the synthetic user prompt and short framing messages around already selected native tool pairs. Disabling tool truncation preserves every receipt byte-for-byte for rebuilding.


source

mk_template
def mk_template(
    picked, # Native custom call/result pairs
    opening:str='Bootstrapping: I read the tooling docs, check the catalog, then take the dojo.', # Reply text preceding the first tool call
    closing:str="OK I'm ready.", # Reply text ending the round
):
A template dialog with native tool output left untruncated



tdlg = mk_template(mini, opening='Practice first.')
test_eq(tdlg.messages[0].content, TMPL_PROMPT)
back = dlg2items(tdlg)
call = first(x for x in back if x.get('type')=='custom_tool_call')
test_eq(parse_exec(call['input']).arguments['code'], 'dojo_start()')

The packaged dialog and store must agree, since the store is compiled from the dialog. Read that reviewed artifact through the same conversion path and reject it if its calls, score, or completion receipt no longer survive the round trip.

packaged = read_ipynb(str(files('llmdojo')/'dojo_data'/'dojo_template.ipynb'))
packaged_items = dlg2items(packaged)
assert dojo_cid(packaged_items)
test_eq(is_clean(packaged_items), [])



Compact sample
The package also carries the substantive calls from the completed round as a compact sample session. Startup, kata-control, and scoring calls are omitted; very high token limits retain the captured arguments and results.


source

dojo_sample
def dojo_sample(
    src
):
The completed dojo’s substantive calls rendered as a compact sample session



sample = dojo_sample(packaged_items)
test('doc(find_msgs, view_dlg)', sample, in_)
test('```python', sample, in_)
for omitted in ('dojo_start()', 'dojo_score(', '# kata', '%cd '): assert omitted not in sample
len(sample)

11137


Regenerate the packaged sample after replacing the reviewed Codex template.

sample_path = Path(files('llmdojo')/'dojo_data'/'codexdojo_sample.md')
sample_path.write_text(dojo_sample(packaged_items))
sample_path

title: codexdojo
text:
Template store
The store keeps native Responses items plus the clean-round completion id, dojo version, and documented-tool state. It is package data, compiled from the canonical dialog by dojobuild and shipped with the code, so updating llmdojo updates the template with nothing per-user to rebuild.
save_template writes native items and the metadata needed to replay them: completion id, dojo version, and documented-tool state.


source

save_template
def save_template(
    items, # Curated native template items
    d:NoneType=None, # Store dir; `TMPL_DIR` if None
):
Write the template and its metadata to the store


load_template reads that pair of files without converting the items through another representation.


source

load_template
def load_template(
    d:NoneType=None, # Store dir; `TMPL_DIR` if None
):
The stored native items and metadata



store = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
save_template(dlg2items(tdlg),store)
stored,meta = load_template(store)
test_eq(meta,dict(cid='ab12',v=_dojo_v()))
test_eq(dojo_cid(stored),'ab12')

build_template is the reverse review path: convert an edited dialog to native items, regenerate ids, and update the store.


source

build_template
def build_template(
    src, # Path to a template dialog
    d:NoneType=None, # Store dir; `TMPL_DIR` if None
):
Convert a reviewed template dialog back into the native store



review = store/'review.ipynb'
write_ipynb(tdlg,review)
rebuilt = store/'rebuilt'
build_template(review,rebuilt)
test_eq(dojo_cid(load_template(rebuilt)[0]),'ab12')

title: codexdojo
text:
Launching
Creating a dojo session starts a Codex thread, injects the native template, registers its completion receipt, and seeds the documented-tool state. Appending performs the same injection at the tail of an existing thread after compaction.

Starting a thread
prep_dojo creates a persisted Codex thread, injects a freshly re-id’d copy of the template, registers its completion, and seeds the matching documentation receipts.


source

prep_dojo
async def prep_dojo(
    cwd:NoneType=None, # Project to start in; current directory if None
    d:NoneType=None, # Template store dir; `TMPL_DIR` if None
    codex_home:NoneType=None, # Alternate Codex home, primarily for tests
):
Create a thread containing the template and return its id




Refreshing after compaction
append_dojo appends a fresh copy of the worked round to an existing thread and changes only its synthetic prompt to explain why the exercise is repeating.


source

append_dojo
async def append_dojo(
    sid:NoneType=None, # Thread id to append to; newest thread for the project if None
    cwd:NoneType=None, # Project directory; current directory if None
    d:NoneType=None, # Template store dir; `TMPL_DIR` if None
    codex_home:NoneType=None, # Alternate Codex home
):
Append the template to an existing thread and return its id


append_dojo is the post-compaction repair. Native compaction replaces the worked history with a summary, so appending restores the demonstrations at the tail and merges their documented-tool state. Re-salting ids makes repeated repairs safe.
The app-server integration runs against an isolated CODEX_HOME, with no model turn: prepare the round and read the thread back as a dialog:

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
    home,proj = Path(td),Path(td)/'project'
    proj.mkdir()
    sid = await prep_dojo(proj,store,home)
    back = thread2dlg(sid,home,mx=None)
    assert any(m.msg_type=='prompt' and m.content==TMPL_PROMPT for m in back.messages)
    test_eq(is_clean(active_items(load_rollout(sid,home))),[])



Compacting with the DSL
Native Codex compaction is encrypted and needs a model turn; llmsurgery.oai.compact_session instead writes a readable compact-DSL document straight into the rollout, offline. compact_dojo chains the two steps — dsl-compact the thread with earlier rounds stripped out of the document, then append a fresh round — so codexdojo -c resumes a session that is both short and re-demonstrated:
The DSL compact should carry the conversation’s work, not its warm-up: the fresh round appended afterwards supersedes any earlier one. As on the Claude side, a round occupies whole user turns, so strip_dojo chunks the items with the shared _turns and drops the turns that dealt a round; compact_session’s strip hook applies it before anything is compacted. A thread holding nothing but rounds is compacted whole rather than emptied.


source

strip_dojo
def strip_dojo(
    items, # Responses items in conversation order
):
Copy of items without the user turns that dealt a round (bare dojo_start())


_strip guards the compaction: when stripping would leave nothing to compact, the round stays:

work = custom_turn('What season is it?', 'tools.mcp__clikernel__py', dict(code='season()'), 'winter', 'Winter.')
played = custom_turn('Play the round.', 'tools.mcp__clikernel__py', dict(code='dojo_start()'), '== llmdojo ==', 'Underway.')
test_eq(strip_dojo(work+played+work), work+work)
test_eq(_strip(played), played)
[item_txt(x) for x in _strip(work+played) if x.get('type')=='message']

['What season is it?', 'Winter.']




source

compact_dojo
async def compact_dojo(
    sid:NoneType=None, # Thread id to compact; newest thread for the project if None
    cwd:NoneType=None, # Project directory; current directory if None
    d:NoneType=None, # Template store dir; `TMPL_DIR` if None
    codex_home:NoneType=None, # Alternate Codex home
):
Synthetically compact a thread with the compact DSL (previous dojo rounds removed first), then append the template round; returns its id


The same isolated app-server setup drives the offline compaction end to end: prepare the round, append real work through the app server, then compact_dojo:

home = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
proj = home/'project'
proj.mkdir()
sid = await prep_dojo(proj,store,home)
work = custom_turn('What season is it?','tools.mcp__clikernel__py',dict(code='season()'),'winter','Winter.')
async with codex_client(home) as codex: await codex.append_thread(sid,work)
test_eq(await compact_dojo(sid,proj,store,home), sid)

The compact document keeps the real work and drops the dealt round. Codex records fresh context items at resume, ahead of the injected round. The compacted thread still gates clean:

prior,new = split_compaction(load_rollout(sid,home))
body = item_txt(prior[-1])
assert 'dojo_start()' not in body
test('season()', body, in_)
assert any(item_txt(o)==APPEND_PROMPT for o in new)
test_eq(is_clean(active_items(load_rollout(sid,home))),[])
shutil.rmtree(home)



Command line
A call_parse CLI mirroring claudedojo’s (the capitalized params declare the short flags: Resume → -r, Compact → -c): every mode prepares a thread and then execs codex resume on it, with standing arguments from launch_config('codex') (the codex_args list in $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/codexdojo/config.toml) and anything the launcher doesn’t recognize forwarded via nested=True. The id comes right after resume, so a stray forwarded token lands in codex’s optional prompt slot rather than stealing the session id; forwarded flag values still need --flag=value form, and the fresh-launch path rejects a stray sess loudly. --sid prints the prepared id and exits. Store builds live in dojobuild.


source

main
def main(
    sess:str=None, # Thread id; the project's newest where omitted
    Resume:bool=False, # Append the round to an existing thread after compaction, then resume it
    Compact:bool=False, # Synthetically compact the thread with the compact DSL, then append the round and resume

    capture:bool=False, # Run a clean round in a bare Codex child and store it
    current:bool=False, # Store the clean round an existing thread already played (`capture_current`)
):
Prepare a Codex thread opening with the worked round and launch codex resume on it; template maintenance is dojobuild

title: claudesub
text:
Claude Code’s own subagents share their parent’s clikernel kernel, and a fork re-reads the parent’s whole context on every turn. claudesub gives a session a different kind of helper: a claude -p child whose history is the parent’s transcript rendered as a compact document (llmsurgery’s compaction DSL, a fraction of the tokens with the decisions and evidence kept), running in its own process and so its own kernel. The parent launches it from a background Bash call or a Monitor, reads its text as it works, and can resume it with an answer if it stops to ask. This is Claude Code only: it composes fastclaude.session, llmsurgery.ant.prepare_compaction, and the dojo’s completion registry.
from fastcore.test import *
import shutil, tempfile

title: claudesub
text:
The parent session
The launching session is named by CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID in the Bash tool’s environment, which we verified matches the transcript stem in interactive sessions, subagents, and -p children alike. When it is unset, or names no transcript, parent_sid refuses rather than guessing: compacting the wrong conversation into a child would be a silent error. The child also needs a dojo completion id to skip the round: the newest one minted under the current tooling version.


source

dojo_cid
def dojo_cid():
The newest clean-round completion id minted under the current dojo version, or None




source

parent_sid
def parent_sid(
    cwd:NoneType=None, # Project directory; the current directory if None
):
The launching session, from CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID; an error rather than a guess when it is unset or names no transcript



os.environ['CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID'] = 'not-a-session'
test_fail(parent_sid, contains='not-a-session')
del os.environ['CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID']
test_fail(parent_sid, contains='CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID')


cid = dojo_cid()
assert cid is None or len(cid)==4
cid

title: claudesub
text:
The child session
The child does not get a copy of the parent’s transcript. prepare_compaction renders the parent’s conversation into the compact document and builds the five records Claude Code writes for a compaction (boundary, summary, and the visible /compact exchange); prep_sub saves just those as a new session, under the same project: a headless resume does not look beyond its own project directory. Resuming it loads only what follows the boundary, so the child’s context is the compact document plus whatever the harness injects live. A synthetic parent shows the shape:


source

prep_sub
def prep_sub(
    sid:NoneType=None, # Parent session id; `parent_sid()` if None
    cwd:NoneType=None, # Project directory; the current directory if None
):
Write a session holding only the parent’s compacted history, returning its id for the child to resume



mproj = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
turns = tool_turn('Which module handles retries?', 'mcp__clikernel__py', dict(code="rg('retry', 'src')"),
    'src/api.py:12:def with_retry(', 'Retries live in src/api.py.', cwd=mproj)
psid = save_sess(turns, cwd=mproj)
csid = prep_sub(psid, mproj)
child = load_sess(csid, mproj)
test_ne(csid, psid)
test_eq(child[0].subtype, 'compact_boundary')
assert child[1].isCompactSummary and 'retry' in rec_txt(child[1])
test_eq({r.sessionId for r in child}, {csid})
[r.type for r in child]

title: claudesub
text:
The protocol and the command
The child’s standing instructions ride in --append-system-prompt, so they never enter its transcript and are identical for every child: what it is, that its kernel is its own, that nobody will answer a question mid-task, how the parent resumes it, and which dojo id to present. Everything else is the directive. Standing claude arguments come from the same launch_config('claude') that claudedojo reads, and a caller’s extra flags follow them.


source

sub_cmd
def sub_cmd(
    directive, # The child's task
    sid, # Session id for the child to resume
    cid:NoneType=None, # Dojo completion id to hand the child; `dojo_cid()` if None
    extra:tuple=(), # Further `claude` arguments, after the standing ones from `launch_config`
):
argv for the headless child: resume sid with directive, streaming events as JSON lines; refuses without a clean-round id, since a child never plays the round



argv = sub_cmd('Summarize src/api.py', csid, cid='ab12', extra=['--model=haiku'])
test_eq(argv[:3], ['claude', '-p', 'Summarize src/api.py'])
assert f'--resume={csid}' in argv and argv[-1]=='--model=haiku'
assert "dojo_start('ab12')" in argv[argv.index('--append-system-prompt')+1]
os.environ['LLMDOJO_STATE_DIR'] = tempfile.mkdtemp()
test_fail(lambda: sub_cmd('x', csid), contains='play one in the parent session')
del os.environ['LLMDOJO_STATE_DIR']
argv[3:6]

title: claudesub
text:
Running the child
run_sub runs the command and prints each text part the child emits as it arrives, which is the child’s own narration at its own rhythm, then a footer naming the child’s session, turn count, and cost. Under a background Bash call that output lands in the task’s file; under a Monitor each line is an event. The result event comes back for the caller; a child that exits without one is an error, not a silent success.


source

run_sub
def run_sub(
    argv, # The child command, from `sub_cmd`
    quiet:bool=False, # Print only the final report and footer, not the child's text as it arrives?
    cwd:NoneType=None, # Directory the child runs in; the current directory if None
):
Run the child, streaming its text, and return its result event


A live run (real model spend, so eval: false) proves the child truly starts from the compacted history: it answers from facts that exist only in the synthetic parent above.

res = run_sub(sub_cmd('From the history only: which file holds the retries? Reply in one line.', csid, extra=['--model=haiku']), cwd=mproj)
assert 'api.py' in res['result']

title: claudesub
text:
The command line
claudesub 'directive' is the whole parent-side API, and -r <child-sid> 'answer' continues a child that stopped to ask, keeping its context. As with claudedojo, nested=True forwards unrecognized flags to claude in --flag=value form, so --model=haiku or --max-turns=20 need no wrapper support. A failed child exits non-zero, which the background task notification reports.


source

main
def main(
    directive:str, # The child's task
    Resume:str=None, # A child session id to continue with `directive` as its next prompt, instead of spawning from this session
    sid:bool=False, # Print the prepared child session id instead of launching
    Quiet:bool=False, # Print only the child's final report, not its progress text
    cwd:str=None, # Project directory to work from, for the parent lookup, the child session, and the child itself; the current directory if None
):
Spawn a headless Claude child on this session’s compacted history and stream its text; unrecognized --flag=value args go to claude
